pageCache.text:
The Children Come First
Welcome to Highwood Copse Primary School
Highwood Copse Primary School provides the best academic, creative, spiritual, moral, and emotional education possible, striving for excellence in all that we do.
Set upon lush grounds, with an ancient body of woodland just beyond, Highwood Copse Primary School boasts picturesque views and enviable facilities. There is space to run, dream and contemplate. Friendships for life will be born overlooking the lake, ambitions will emerge from the classrooms.
Book an Open Day
NEWSLETTERS
Our Vision
Highwood Copse Primary School will provide the best academic, creative, spiritual, moral and emotional education possible, striving for excellence in all that we do.
Our school is a place where the children are central to every decision we make. We will ensure our children are safe and successful; they will grow during their time with us to be ambitious and resilient. We are proud that our children are learning to be courageously outspoken, but behave with integrity. The staff and school will be highly effective, well-organised, efficient, and well-resourced. We will provide an exciting and stimulating learning environment and our talented, well-informed teachers will inspire and motivate children, encouraging scholarship, intellectual curiosity, independent thought and effective learning habits. Children will be encouraged to celebrate Britain as a diverse society, have an understanding of social justice, fight against discrimination, provide service for others, and show respectful and well-informed views about their own community and the wider world.
Testimonials
“I just wanted to say thank you so much for giving us the opportunity to come and spend time with our children in class. It was a great experience and lovely to see the class enjoying their maths lesson so much (and listening so beautifully to Miss Newman’s instructions)!”
'We do want to say how amazed we are with the school! Ivy-Rose adores school and I never thought this would be the case!
How much she learns and takes in the information and comes home and shares everything with us all is amazing. The education that she’s receiving is the best and has wowed us as parents. My 5 year old is enjoying learning! Something you never think you’d say till later down her school education. The smiles that each staff member has at all times welcoming the children and saying goodbye at the end of the day is not known in many schools and is very much appreciated. The fact all the staff we’ve met has known her name is incredible too. I’ve worked in childcare for 16 years in many schools and we couldn’t have picked a better one to send our baby too! I’d like to commend Mrs Robinson on the school she has created and the warm loving staff members she has. The relationship you clearly have with your staff is second to none because everyone’s on it and the fact I don’t know another school with a head teacher that is so highly involved with their children and parents is a credit to you too. So thank you.'

pageCache.pageTitle: Highwood Copse Primary School - WRAPAROUND CARE
pageCache.text:
Breakfast and After School Clubs
Early Birds Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club – 8am to start of school day £4.50 per session held in Early Birds Club.
Breakfast will be served from 8am to 8:25am.
Night Owls After School Club
After school club for all year groups from Reception to Year 5 is led by Mrs King and runs after school until 5.30pm Monday - Thursdays and until 5pm on a Friday.
Any enquiries relating to wraparound care clubs can be made to admin@highwoodcopse.co.uk
Places for both clubs are allocated termly in accordance with our terms and conditions.

pageCache.pageTitle: Highwood Copse Primary School - SCHOOL UNIFORM AND PE KIT
pageCache.text:
School Uniform and PE Kit
Winter School Uniform
Tie, striped blue, silver and purple
Tailored trousers, skirt or pinafore - charcoal grey in colour
Long or short sleeved blue shirt
Purple knitted cardigan or jumper, embroidered with logo
Grey socks or tights
Comfortable black shoes, which the children can put on and remove independently
Summer School Uniform
Tie, striped blue, silver and purple.
Tailored trousers, skirt and pinafore - grey in colour.
Optional grey shorts or purple gingham summer dress.
Long or short sleeved blue shirt.
Purple knitted cardigan or jumper, embroidered with logo.
Grey socks or tights.
Comfortable black shoes, which the children can put on and
remove independently.
PE Kit
Purple T-shirt, printed with school logo
A separate pair of grey or white socks
In winter, the children should bring a black tracksuit to wear over their PE kit in the event of outdoor PE.
The kit should be bought to school in the purple PE bag, embroidered with the school logo. Sometimes, the opportunity to do sports arises spontaneously, so it's a good idea to have a PE kit in school at all times.
We care passionately that the children come to school looking and feeling their best. While there is a place for jewellery, fund hair colours, nail polish and bold hair styles and colours, this place is not at school.
The exception to this is one smaller ear stud in both or either ear, which will need to be removed for PE and any other sports activities for health and safety reasons and in line with UK sports bodies regulations. If your Highwoodian is wearing PE kit for the day we request they do not wear earings to school on that day.
To prevent newly pierced ears from closing up when studs are removed, we request that you confirm your child to having their ears pierced during the long summer break.
Our school uniform, PE kit and book bags can be purchased from SkoolKit in Newbury or online via Skoolkit.

pageCache.pageTitle: Highwood Copse Primary School - Book an Open Day
pageCache.text:
Book an Open Day
We hold two talks in September with our Principal, Serraphina Robinson, we strongly recommend attending a talk, as it is one of the most informative ways to learn more about Highwood Copse. The dates and times of the talks will be put on the homepage of the website in early September.
In late September we will release our School Tour dates, please keep an eye on the website for these dates and all the relevant information on how to book onto them. There will be plenty of available dates and times when we release these.
For any mid year admissions we will only offer school tours if we have space available in that year group. Please check with West Berkshire Admissions to confirm if there is space and if there is a waiting list.

pageCache.pageTitle: Highwood Copse Primary School - MUSIC CURRICULUM
pageCache.text:
Music
At Highwood Copse, we enable children to feel that they are musical and develop a life-long love of music. Our focus is on developing the skills, knowledge and understanding children need in order to become confident composers, performers and listeners. Our curriculum introduces children to all forms of music from around the world and fosters a respect of those music traditions. Children develop their musical skills through our robust curriculum based on the Model Music Curriculum, with additional emphasis on the Kodaly and Dalcrose music teaching methods in Foundation stage and KS1. Children have opportunities to sing, play tuned and untuned instruments, improvise and compose, learn to read various forms of music notation, listen and respond to music in their weekly lessons with a specialist music teacher.
All children including those with SEND and who are entitled to PP have varied opportunities to perform, listen to, review and evaluate music across a range of historical periods, genres, styles and traditions.
At Highwood Copse we follow the Model Music Curriculum (non-statutory guidance for music teaching) that sets out sequences of learning in the following areas that all contribute towards an increasing development of musicianship:
Listening
Composing
Performing/Instrument performance.

pageCache.pageTitle: Highwood Copse Primary School - VISIONS AND VALUES
pageCache.text:
Vision & Values
THE CHILDREN COME FIRST
At Highwood Copse, we vow to deliver a holistic education that never falls short of excellence—an education rooted in purpose, tempered by courage, and honed with precision.
To be a Highwoodian is to live our values not only in the classroom but in every decision, conversation, and quiet act beyond our gates. Our Ethos is no ornament; it is the pulse of our community. We approach learning—with integrity, resilience, discipline, gratitude, and generosity—because that is how we learn to live.
We uphold the highest standards not for accolade but in reverence for the children we serve. Every choice begins with a single question: What is best for the child? The future will be cast in their hands; our duty is to forge character and impart skills and knowledge equal to the task. Character is earned—through challenge and compassion, through missteps, safety, and belonging. Academic mastery, while not the whole, is the firm ground from which freedom is launched.
We build an exemplary curriculum and environment designed not merely to educate but to awaken. Highwoodians leave us not only knowing who they are, but knowing that the world does not shape them—they shape the world. Their dreams may shift, their paths may twist, but they will move forward with clarity, courage, and conviction.
Not just prepared for life—prepared to lead it.
At Highwood Copse, our vision is not confined to words on a page—it is made manifest in the way we teach, lead, and grow. Here is how our ethos comes to life:
At Highwood Copse, the vision becomes real in every lesson, every gesture, every child who walks through our gates—and walks back out ready to shape the world
